text.p: Gruntal & Co said on Monday it raised its rating on the shares of Bristol-Myers Squibb Co to a strong buy from a buy, based on the company's new products.
-- Analyst David Saks said in a research note he raised his 1997 earnings estimate to $3.20 per share from $3.17 per share and his 1998 earnings estimate to $3.65 per share from $3.60 per share.
-- Saks said he raised his one-year price target to $105 per share from $81.

-- "We see Bristol now entering a new era of accelerated growth," he said. "This new growth is fueled by the breakout of many new products, core brand leaders and a strong triple-A financial condition."

-- New products which are expected to drive future growth for Bristol-Myers include irbesartan for high blood pressure; clopidogrel to prevent heart attack, stroke and arterial disease; and UFT for prostate cancer, he said.
-- The stock was trading down 13/16 at 81-1/4.
